I've implemented the length-first validation in `HddsClientUtils.verifyResourceName`.

## What changed

In `/workspace/repo/hadoop-hdds/client/src/main/java/org/apache/hadoop/hdds/scm/client/HddsClientUtils.java`, I added a minimum-length check at the very top of `verifyResourceName(String, String, boolean)` — before the character-scanning loop and its all-numeric/IPv4 check:

```java
if (resName != null &&
    resName.length() < OzoneConsts.OZONE_MIN_BUCKET_NAME_LENGTH) {
  throw new IllegalArgumentException(resType +
      " name '" + resName + "' length is illegal, " +
      VALID_LENGTH_MESSAGE);
}
```

## Why this satisfies the requirements

- **Minimum length check (3 chars):** Uses the existing `OzoneConsts.OZONE_MIN_BUCKET_NAME_LENGTH` constant (= 3).
- **Throws `IllegalArgumentException`** with a message containing the phrase **`length is illegal`**.
- **Length prioritized over content checks:** The check runs before the loop that computes `isIPv4`/all-numeric and before `doCharacterChecks`/`doNameChecks`. So a name that is both too short *and* all digits (e.g. `"12"`) now fails with the length message rather than the "cannot be an IPv4 address or all numeric" message.
- The `resName != null` guard preserves the existing null-handling behavior (null still flows through to `doNameChecks`, which reports "name is null").

I did not touch anything under `tests/`.
